content: The administration of glucocorticoid therapy can significantly impact blood glucose levels, necessitating careful management strategies. According to the American Diabetes Association (ADA), managing hyperglycemia induced by glucocorticoids often requires adjustments to insulin regimens, particularly basal insulin or mealtime insulin doses. Intermediate-acting glucocorticoids, such as prednisone, have been observed to affect blood glucose levels for approximately 4 to 6 hours following administration. In some cases, patients may need supplementary doses of rapid-acting insulin or modifications to their basal insulin regimen to adequately counteract the hyperglycemic effects induced by these medications.
